name: sandbox-terminal
changelog: v5: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager signs its fake coding agent in with the agent's own login command and can take a smaller stdin limit — nothing changes for people or managers. v4: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager offers the contract's optional stdio capability (a split exec's stderr apart, a non-tty exec's streams on one WebSocket) — nothing changes for people or managers. v3: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager advertises an image's coding agents (hello.images[].harnesses) and gives a terminal TERM, COLORTERM and LANG — nothing changes for people or managers. v2: its tests' copy of the fake sandbox manager follows the contract's optional ports capability (D135) — nothing changes for people or managers. v1: terminals onto coding sandboxes for people, over the sandbox-manager contract — its page lists the sandboxes shared with it by manager and opens browser terminals straight to the manager as tabs (reattaching to running ones, ending them), and SSH (ssh <sandbox>@host -p 2222) with keys registered per person on the page — every login asks xbind whether the key's person still has access to the tile (removed or disabled: access revoked, their keys kept inactive); a native view lists them and manages keys (terminals open in the browser); sandboxes reach it by being shared with it
title: Sandbox terminals
description: Terminals onto coding sandboxes for people, in the browser and over SSH. Bind it to one or more sandbox managers (the coding-sandbox template, or any tile implementing /docs/sandbox-manager.md); a sandbox shows up here once its owner shares it with this tile. People register their SSH public keys on its page and log in with ssh <sandbox>@host -p 2222 after an admin publishes the port (bx expose apps/sandbox-terminal ssh=runtime --listen :2222). No port forwarding, agent forwarding or sftp.
